claims.text: Applying ALD at approximately 200–250 °C can deposit a conformal 5–10 nm copper coating on each tungsten particle.
The low ALD temperature avoids thermal damage to the material.
The copper coating forms a nanometer-scale conformal interlayer at W–Cu interfaces after consolidation.
The ALD copper interlayer enhances the wettability of tungsten during SPS.
The ALD copper coating eliminates detrimental interfacial oxides.
Enhanced wetting and elimination of interfacial oxides produce nearly perfect atomic contact between tungsten and copper.
Nearly perfect W–Cu contact minimizes interfacial void formation and defects.
Reduced interfacial voids yield a more uniform and well-integrated W–Cu composite microstructure.
The resulting microstructure improves thermal transport.
The resulting microstructure improves mechanical durability under thermal stresses and irradiation associated with fusion-reactor joints.
ALD-coated tungsten particles processed by SPS will have fewer interfacial voids than uncoated tungsten particles processed by SPS.
The ALD-coated approach will produce greater microstructural uniformity than uncoated-powder SPS.
The ALD-coated approach will outperform vapor-coated tungsten powder approaches in interfacial void reduction, uniformity, mechanical durability, and thermal transport.
SPS at around 900 °C and approximately 50 MPa in vacuum or inert gas is an appropriate consolidation regime for the proposed ALD-coated W–Cu material.
The ultrathin copper interlayer can remain effective through SPS and subsequent fusion-relevant thermal and irradiation exposure.
